english.title: Member of the house of commons attempt to provide false / misleading information for allowances claim
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a member of the House of Commons of the United Kingdom Parliament representing the constituency of **(..SPECIFY THE CONSTITUENCY..), attempted to make a claim under the members of parliament allowances scheme and provide information for the purposes of the claim knowing it to be false or misleading in a material respect, namely **(..SPECIFY FALSE / MISLEADING MATERIAL..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 10 of the Parliamentary Standards Act 2009 and section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Either way - Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

In relation to offences committed before 2nd May 2022, the reference to twelve months is to be read as six months (section 10(3)(a) of the Parliamentary Standards Act 2009).

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
